places.chef: second-generation owner-operator · Himeji, Hyogo, Japan · Teishu traces its roots to roughly 60 years ago when it opened as Yougetsu Shokudo (ようげつ食堂) near the Himeji Civic Hall (市民会館). The founder chose the name 停主 — meaning something like 'a host who bids guests to pause and rest' — to express a philosophy of unhurried welcome. The current owner is the second generation. The shop stood for decades on a lane facing Himeji Castle until an April 2024 fire destroyed the building completely. With no insurance payout (coverage had lapsed because the adjuster handling renewal was hospitalized), the owner relied on community support — including a charity T-shirt campaign at ¥4,000 per piece — and his son's help to clear the site and begin reconstruction. In May 2025 he reopened in a makeshift outdoor space on the parking lot, described by visitors as evoking a nostalgic Showa-era beer garden atmosphere. As of mid-2026 the kitchen is still serving from that temporary setup while the permanent rebuild awaits Cultural Affairs Agency clearance, required because the site lies along the official approach path to Himeji Castle. · Traditional homestyle cooking rooted in place — the kind of food …

Celiacs should avoid unless they can clearly communicate needs in Japanese and staff confirm wheat-free substitution is possible, which is unlikely given the core broth.
